explanation.headline: Bet 1 bb was the top play, and you found it.

paragraphs: You held 6♣ 8♣ on the button, against Villain, a LAG player, in the big blind. Pre-flop, you opened to 2.5 bb and Villain called.
The flop came 4♥ 3♥ 3♠: Villain checked. It was your turn to act with 5 bb in the pot.
sections.title: The hand

paragraphs: You chose Bet 1 bb (EV 2.22 bb), which matched or beat the top listed play (Bet 33%) against Villain's range. Verdict: Best.
Your equity against Villain's whole range is 24.9%.

Bet 33%: Villain folds 41% of the time, more than the 23.1% a bet this size needs to profit on folds alone (1.5 bb / (5 bb + 1.5 bb)), so the folds alone pay for it, even when every hand that continues beats you. On top of that, you have 23.2% equity against the hands that continue. Bet 1 bb: Villain folds 39% of the time, more than the 16.7% a bet this size needs to profit on folds alone (1 bb / (5 bb + 1 bb)), so the folds alone pay for it, even when every hand that continues beats you. On top of that, you have 23.3% equity against the hands that continue.
Right now you are ahead of 8.8% of Villain's range. The largest parts of the range are Air (31.9% of it; your equity 28%) and Weak made hand (31.2% of it; your equity 24%).
sections.title: The verdict

paragraphs: Villain is a LAG player. Loose-aggressive: wide ranges, frequent pressure, more bluffs.
Villain's range narrowed with each action: Pre-flop: calls; Flop: checks.
The range in the Range tab is the range this puzzle was graded on.
